title: Held, Not Touched
logline: A gem-cutter brings a rough stone close under a single lamp and looks at it for far longer than seems reasonable, until both its flaws and its worth become visible.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: One plain object for each person becomes one stone held under one lamp for longer than seems reasonable, until its faults and its worth both show.

thread_out.thread: Attention held on one thing grows finer: a potter throwing nested bowls, each wall thinner than the last, stopping just before thinner would mean broken.

requirements: A working gem-cutter willing to be filmed over a real commission
Good light control for close macro photography
Time to follow one stone through several sessions

suggestions.name: Ratnapura
suggestions.why: Sri Lanka's best-known gem-trading and cutting town.
suggestions.access_notes: Many small workshops; a specific willing cutter must be found.
suggestions.verify: Access to a specific workshop and cutter is unverified.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Ordinary attention only brushes past things, but attention that stays on one thing for a long time begins to see it clearly. The texts picture someone bringing an object close and looking at it until everything about it is plain.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සාමාන්‍ය අවධානය දේවල් යන්තමින් ස්පර්ශ කර ඉදිරියට යයි, නමුත් එකම දෙයක් ළඟට ගෙන දිගු වේලාවක් නොසැලී බලා සිටින විට එය පැහැදිලිව පෙනෙන්නට පටන් ගනී.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts describe the minds of meditative absorption (jhāna) as gripping their object firmly, as if embracing it, where ordinary sense-sphere minds take it only lightly. The Pradeepika's image is someone who wants to examine something well: they keep it close, send the mind nowhere else, and look for a long time until it appears clearly. As absorption deepens, the mind grows simpler, dropping applied thought, then sustained thought, then rapture. Real skill, the texts add, means being able to enter such a state, stay as long as one wishes, leave and review it at will.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows one rough stone from its first slow turn under the lamp to the finished cut, and lets the length of the looking be felt. As the cutter settles, talk and movement thin out while the rest of the room goes on unnoticed. Rejected angles and the first facet catching light let the viewer see worth appearing only after a long, undistracted look.

key_terms.en: masteries: adverting, attaining, resolving duration, emerging, reviewing

lesson.caution: The film makes no claim about the cutter's inner state: skilled focus in a craft is only an echo of absorption, which the texts describe as a trained meditative state withdrawn from sense desire, not flow at work.
lesson.builds_on: Where the class gave each person one plain object, this film shows what the texts say happens when attention stays on a single object for a long time.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
